rubrics.justification: Description is consistent with a Day 5 expanded blastocyst and the provided 3AB grade, with appropriate comments on blastocoel, zona thinning, compact ICM, and looser TE. Minor overreach includes assigning some features not clearly verifiable from a single image and slight ambiguity between grade 3 and 3-4 wording.
Thoroughly integrates age, ovarian reserve, male factor diagnosis, sperm parameters, endometrial thickness, BMI, and first-cycle status with embryo quality and prognosis.

Overall logic is clear and internally consistent, and the prognosis follows from embryo grade and patient factors. Minor issues include a few speculative claims (e.g., paternal DNA repair implications, protocol comparisons, first-cycle advantage) stated with more certainty than warranted.

Recommendations are largely consistent with IVF practice, especially support for single embryo transfer in a young patient with a good-quality blastocyst. Small deviations include overstatement of ERA/acupuncture-related points and some nonessential procedural specifics not directly guideline-driven.
Provides clear next-step recommendations for transfer strategy, luteal support, contingency planning after failure, and future embryo banking/FET considerations, with practical case-specific detail.
